questions.q: What does the `connectVia` property on the on-premises SQL linked service actually do?
options: Routes the connection through the self-hosted integration runtime bridging into the on-premises network
Encrypts the connection string automatically
Schedules when the linked service can be used
Has no functional effect — it's purely cosmetic
questions.explain: connectVia points the linked service at the self-hosted IR, which is what actually lets Data Factory reach a SQL Server sitting inside the on-premises network.

questions.q: Why does the linked service store its connection string as an AzureKeyVaultSecret reference instead of a plain string?
options: To satisfy the "no passwords in plain text" security requirement from the very first linked service built
Because SQL Server linked services don't support plain connection strings at all
It's required syntax with no functional purpose
To make the pipeline run faster
questions.explain: Building security in from the first linked service — rather than as an afterthought — directly satisfies Lesson 53's requirement about not exposing credentials in plain text.

questions.q: What does the sqlReaderQuery in the Copy activity's source filter to?
options: Exactly yesterday's orders, using a date filter on OrderDate
The entire Sales.Orders table, every single run
Only orders from the current calendar year
Nothing — sqlReaderQuery has no filtering capability
questions.explain: The query filters to OrderDate equal to yesterday's date, deliberately avoiding copying the entire historical table on every run.

questions.q: Why was Parquet chosen for the raw zone sink instead of CSV?
options: Columnar storage for efficient column-subset reads, embedded schema, and native compatibility with Spark/OneLake
Parquet is the only format Copy activities support
CSV files can't be stored in ADLS Gen2 at all
Parquet requires no schema, unlike CSV
questions.explain: Parquet's columnar layout, embedded schema, and broad compatibility with tools like Spark make it a deliberate choice for a raw zone that downstream transformations will read from selectively.

questions.q: What are the three concrete verification steps for confirming this pipeline stage actually works?
options: Run it manually, confirm exactly one new file lands with the right data, and check the schema via Preview data
Just check that the pipeline shows "Succeeded" in the Monitor hub, nothing more
Wait a week and see if anyone complains
Verification isn't necessary if the pipeline was built correctly
questions.explain: The lesson's concrete bar goes beyond a green checkmark: confirming the right file landed with the right data and schema, verified directly rather than assumed.
